metadata.title: PISA 2022 insights on intellectual curiosity, perspective-taking, and science achievement: Examining the mediating pathways
metadata.venue: International Journal of Educational Research Open

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses secondary microdata from PISA 2022 for science achievement and related questionnaire items, with an analytic sample reduced after outlier screening (from N=24,600 to 21,510). The manuscript does not report whether PISA sampling weights or replicate weights were applied, nor does it name any PISA weight variables. Because the analysis is conducted in SmartPLS 4 using SEM-PLS (bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples), the paper does not provide guidance on weight-aware estimation for the structural paths. Analysts using the PISA dataset should consult the PISA technical documentation for the appropriate student weight (and replicate weights if variance estimation is required) and apply them consistently if population-representative inference is desired.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2022 secondary data for UAE students. The initial dataset comprised N=24,600 responses, then missing-data imputation was performed (EM means reported; Little’s MCAR test used to justify imputation). After imputation, the authors screened for univariate and multivariate outliers: 2,328 univariate outliers and 762 multivariate outliers were removed, leaving 21,510 valid cases for the SEM-PLS measurement and structural model analyses. Items with low outer loadings were removed from constructs (Perspective-taking: ST303Q05JA, ST303Q07JA; Intellectual Curiosity: ST301Q08JA, ST301Q03JA) based on an outer-loading threshold of 0.6.

main_findings.performance_metrics: SEM-PLS path coefficients (bootstrapped): Intellectual curiosity -> Science achievement direct β=0.19 (T=22.57, p=0); Perspective-taking -> Science achievement β=0.15 (T=18.98, p=0); Intellectual curiosity -> Perspective-taking -> Science achievement indirect β=0.09 (T=18.69, p=0); Intellectual curiosity total effect on Science achievement β=0.28 (T=42.96, p=0). R-square for Science achievement=0.09.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Science data for UAE students, the study leveraged Intellectual curiosity and Perspective-taking to predict Science achievement, finding that both Intellectual curiosity (direct β=0.19) and Perspective-taking (β=0.15) were significant predictors, with a significant mediation pathway where Intellectual curiosity also improved Science achievement indirectly via Perspective-taking (indirect β=0.09). This indicates that strengthening students’ intellectual curiosity and explicitly developing perspective-taking skills may improve science achievement, though the cross-sectional SEM-PLS design limits causal interpretation.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2022 secondary data for UAE students (initial N=24,600; reduced to 21,510 after outlier screening) to examine whether intellectual curiosity predicts science achievement and whether perspective-taking mediates this relationship. Missingness was handled using EM-based imputation with Little’s MCAR test indicating non-random missingness (Chi-Square=242,472.600, DF=235,009, Sig.=0.000), and the authors report reliability/validity for the three constructs in a measurement model. Using SmartPLS 4 SEM-PLS with bootstrapping (5,000 resamples), the model shows R-square=0.09 for Science achievement. Intellectual curiosity has a significant direct effect on Science achievement (β=0.19, T=22.57, p=0) and a significant indirect effect through perspective-taking (β=0.09, T=18.69, p=0), while perspective-taking also directly predicts Science achievement (β=0.15, T=18.98, p=0). The paper does not report the use of PISA sampling/replicate weights, and the cross-sectional design constrains causal claims.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction treats the study as non-ML predictive modeling because the analysis is SEM-PLS (SmartPLS 4) with bootstrapped path coefficients and mediation testing rather than training/evaluating machine-learning algorithms. Consequently, ml_techniques.all_techniques is empty and ml_techniques.primary is left null. The paper still provides empirical results (path coefficients, R-square, reliability/validity), but they are structural-equation mediation estimates rather than ML model performance.
